data.title: Implement Data Mapping Logic Layer
data.when: When integrating two modules or services that utilize different underlying data models (e.g., converting a database Entity into a Presentation DTO, or vice versa), but require them to interact as if they were the same type.
procedure: Identify the source structure (A) and the target structure (B).
Define a dedicated Mapper class or interface responsible for the conversion logic from A -> B. Do not mix mapping logic with business service logic.
Implement conversion methods, ensuring all required fields are handled explicitly.
Write comprehensive unit tests for the mapper that cover happy paths, boundary conditions (max/min values), and null inputs.
Update the calling services to accept or return the mapped object type (B) instead of directly passing around the source entity (A).
pitfalls: Writing brittle mapping logic that assumes non-null values, leading to runtime NullPointerExceptions when upstream data is incomplete.
Ignoring bidirectional mapping needs; only implementing A -> B and forgetting B -> A conversion methods.
Violating the Single Responsibility Principle by mixing database fetching/persistence calls into the mapper class itself.
verification: Execute dedicated unit tests for the Mapper class, ensuring that edge cases (empty lists, null inputs) are handled gracefully and correctly mapped to default or optional values.
Run end-to-end integration tests validating that business services can successfully process data using the mapped object without failure.
